skill.name: gif-sticker-maker
skill.description: Create four captioned animated GIF stickers from photos, logos, objects, or pets using MiniMax image and video generation.
skill.summary: Turns photos or logos into a four-sticker animated GIF pack.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: Review found intended MiniMax API calls, environment variable use, file output, and ffmpeg execution. Most static hits are safe implementation patterns, but unrestricted MINIMAX_API_BASE can redirect authorization headers and media to any endpoint if misconfigured. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted MiniMax API base can receive authorization headers and media.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist official MiniMax domains or require explicit confirmation before custom API_BASE values are used.

remediation.issue: Output paths are accepted directly by image, video, and GIF scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict outputs to a workspace directory and reject absolute paths or parent directory traversal.

remediation.issue: The workflow sends prompts, images, and generated media to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Document data handling clearly and ask users before processing private or sensitive images.

content.value_statement: Custom sticker packs can take many manual image and video steps. This skill guides MiniMax image, video, caption, and GIF conversion into one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Generates four static sticker images from a photo or described subject.
Uses MiniMax image generation with optional person reference images.
Animates each sticker through MiniMax image-to-video generation.
Converts MP4 outputs into GIF files with ffmpeg.
Applies short localized captions from the included caption table.
limitations: Requires a MiniMax API key and a configured API base URL.
Requires ffmpeg on the local PATH for GIF conversion.
Subject reference images only support person subjects through the API.
Generated likeness, caption quality, and motion consistency depend on model output.

use_cases.title: Build reaction stickers
use_cases.description: Create a four GIF reaction set from a selfie, product mascot, or logo.

use_cases.title: Localize chat stickers
use_cases.description: Use the caption table to produce stickers in one selected conversation language.

use_cases.title: Prototype mascot animations
use_cases.description: Turn a character concept into quick animated sticker drafts for review.

prompt_templates.title: Use default captions
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner sticker generation from one image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four animated GIF stickers from this photo. Use the default captions for my conversation language.

prompt_templates.title: Provide custom captions
prompt_templates.scenario: User has exact caption text ready.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sticker pack from this image with these captions: Hi, LOL, Boo-hoo, Love ya.

prompt_templates.title: Match a brand mascot
prompt_templates.scenario: Logo or mascot source image needs a sticker set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this logo as the subject. Create four GIF stickers that preserve its colors and simple shape.

prompt_templates.title: Control action and output size
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user wants custom motion and GIF conversion settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four stickers with custom captions and matching actions. Convert the MP4 files to GIF at 12 fps and 320 px wide.

output_examples.input: A user uploads a selfie and asks for default English captions.
output: Four GIF stickers are produced: waving, laughing, crying, and heart gesture.
Each sticker uses a short English caption with readable outlined text.

output_examples.input: A team shares a logo and asks for chat stickers in Spanish.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a mascot-style GIF set with Spanish captions and a clean white background.

output_examples.input: A designer provides a pet photo and four custom phrases.
output_examples.output: The workflow creates four toy-like pet GIFs with the requested phrases matched to actions.

best_practices: Use clear front-facing photos when preserving a person's likeness.
Keep custom captions to one to three short words.
Review generated images before animation to avoid wasting video credits.
anti_patterns: Do not include private images unless third-party API processing is acceptable.
Do not mix languages across captions in the same sticker pack.
Do not use absolute output paths for normal sticker creation.

faq.question: Does this skill need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses MINIMAX_API_KEY and MINIMAX_API_BASE to call MiniMax services.

faq.question: Can it work without ffmpeg?
faq.answer: No. ffmpeg is required to convert MP4 videos into GIF files.

faq.question: How many stickers does it create?
faq.answer: The workflow creates four GIF stickers by default.

faq.question: Can I use my own captions?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide four short captions, and the skill matches actions to their meaning.

faq.question: Does it preserve a person's face?
faq.answer: It can use a subject reference for person photos, but model output may vary.

faq.question: Can it create stickers from logos?
faq.answer: Yes. It can stylize logos into 3D toy-like mascot stickers.
